atoms.a: Think about a saucepan. What material is it made from?

feedback.end: Saucepans made of metal transfer heat quickly from the heat source to the food. The metal conducts the heat.

instruction.text: Read the text and fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Different materials behave ((++differently in_the_same_way)) around electricity. Some materials ((++allow block)) electricity to pass through them. This is called conducting electricity.

instruction.text: Select the sentence parts in the correct order to answer the question.

feedback.finish: Metal and water are examples of conductors of electricity.

instruction.text: Decide if each material is a conductor or not.

trainers.hint: The bulb needs electricity to flow through the circuit in order for it to light up.

feedback.end: Solids, liquids and gases can all conduct electricity. This is why it is important not to use electronics in the bathroom, where they could get wet and become dangerous.

instruction.text: Which image shows air conducting electricity?

feedback.end: For air to conduct electricity, the charge or strength of the electricity needs to be really powerful - like in lightning. Normal plug sockets and electronics don’t contain enough power to conduct through the air, making them safe for us to use.
